structured.school_or_org: Climate Change Commission (CCC) multistakeholder program (with PCW, NRC, private-sector partners)
structured.year_or_edition: PRA modern cycle documented 2023–2025 (third year in 2025); 2026 primer circulated as fourth cycle; earlier Legarda-era PRA existed historically (e.g. 2013 launch references) but is separate from this youth/women cycle
structured.program_event: Philippine Resilience Awards (Women and Youth categories); related CCC youth science track: Climate Science Youth Program / Gawad CCC: Search for Outstanding Young Climate Scientists (public evidence mainly 2018–2019)
structured.theme_or_track: PRA 2024: “Kababaihan at Kabataan: Katatagan ng Bayan”; PRA 2025: “Kababaihan at Kabataan: Katuwang sa Paghahabi ng Isang Matatag na Bayan”; PRA 2026 primer (secondary docs): “Kababaihan at Kabataan: Nagkakaisa Tungo sa Matatag at Maunlad na Pilipinas”; 2023 edition promoted as Philippine Resilience Awards for Women / “Showcasing Gender and …” (full official theme string incomplete in open sources). CCC Week 2024 (host week for PRA, not PRA-only): “Aksyon at Adaptasyon ng Makabagong Henerasyon”. Gawad CCC 2018 congress: “The 1.5 °Celsius Challenge: Securing Water for All Filipinos”; 2019 research focus: Food–Water–Energy Nexus.
structured.what_it_does: PRA is a multistakeholder recognition program led by CCC that nominates, field-validates, and awards women and youth champions whose local initiatives advance climate action and disaster risk reduction/resilience; awardees receive recognition and stated continued support to scale initiatives. Gawad CCC (under Climate Science Youth Program) was a high-school science research contest where students present climate-related research, with regional recognition, bootcamp refinement, and national presentation in coordination with DepEd and NPTE.
structured.place: Philippines (nationwide nominations; ceremonies often Manila / Quezon City during CCC Global Warming and Climate Change Consciousness Week)
structured.outcome_or_award: Women Category and Youth Category champions (e.g. 2025: three women + five youth awardees; cash/support noted in PNA for prior cycles); not a startup accelerator in public materials
structured.theme_same_every_year: No. Across 2023–2026, PRA keeps a stable focus on women and youth (kababaihan at kabataan) and climate/disaster resilience, but the official annual theme wording changes each year (2024 Katatagan ng Bayan; 2025 Katuwang sa Paghahabi ng Isang Matatag na Bayan; 2026 primer Nagkakaisa Tungo sa Matatag at Maunlad na Pilipinas). 2023 was framed more as Awards for Women / gender showcasing. Separate CCC youth science awards (Gawad CCC) also used different topical frames (water security 2018; FWE nexus 2019). No public evidence of one identical theme every year from 2020–2026. No dedicated CCC youth climate “accelerator” with a multi-year fixed theme was found in open sources for this window.
structured.gap: Full official 2023 PRA theme string not captured beyond “for Women” / YouTube “Showcasing Gender and …”. 2026 theme verified only via primer mirrors (Scribd/Studocu), not a live climate.gov.ph press release in this pass. No public multi-year listing of Gawad CCC themes after 2019; program page says “ongoing” but recent award cycles 2020–2026 not found. No CCC-branded youth climate accelerator (vs. awards/recognition) documented in open search for 2020–2026. Exact cash/prize amounts and full winner lists per year not exhaustively verified for every edition.
structured.note: For Youth CLAP / student teams: treat PRA as the main CCC-linked youth climate award with recurring women+youth categories—expect a new Filipino theme each year, not a fixed slogan. Align proposals to climate/DRR resilience and gender-inclusive impact; nominations typically open mid-year with ceremony during CCC Week (November). Do not conflate CCC Week themes with PRA themes (they can differ). Older Gawad CCC is science-high-school research, not an entrepreneurship accelerator. Always re-check climate.gov.ph and PRAwards.PH Facebook for the current year’s official theme and eligibility (youth ages often cited as 15–30 in partner posts).
